quick: 1000 mg twice daily WITH ritonavir 100 mg twice daily (never used alone)
Take within 2 hours after a meal to improve absorption
Use only if clearly needed; limited data, ritonavir boosting required
Breastfeeding not recommended in HIV-positive mothers
No adjustment for mild-moderate; caution in severe impairment
Caution; contraindicated in severe (decompensated) hepatic impairment
Baseline and on-treatment ECG (QT/PR), LFTs, lipids, glucose
summary: Saquinavir is an HIV-1 protease inhibitor used in combination antiretroviral therapy. It must always be co-administered (boosted) with low-dose ritonavir to achieve adequate plasma levels. It carries a notable risk of dose-dependent QT and PR interval prolongation, so a baseline ECG is required and it is contraindicated in patients at risk of serious arrhythmia. It is taken with food and is a substrate/inhibitor of CYP3A4 with many drug interactions.
indications: Treatment of HIV-1 infection in combination with ritonavir and other antiretroviral agents (adults)

dosage.d: Saquinavir 1000 mg + ritonavir 100 mg, both twice daily
dosage.n: Always combined with ritonavir; take within 2 h after a meal

dosage.d: Saquinavir 500 mg + ritonavir 100 mg twice daily for first 7 days, then 1000/100 mg twice daily
dosage.n: Reduced lead-in dose lowers early QT prolongation risk

admin: Always co-administer with ritonavir as a pharmacokinetic booster - never use as sole protease inhibitor
Take within 2 hours after a full meal to ensure adequate absorption
Swallow capsules/tablets whole; complete the dosing as part of combination ART
Obtain a baseline ECG before starting and during treatment
moa: Saquinavir is a selective, competitive inhibitor of HIV-1 and HIV-2 aspartyl protease. By binding the protease active site it prevents cleavage of viral gag-pol polyprotein precursors, producing immature, non-infectious viral particles and halting viral replication.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to saquinavir or any component
Pre-existing complete AV block without pacemaker

Co-administration with drugs that prolong QT/PR or are highly CYP3A4-dependent with serious toxicity (e.g., ergot derivatives, midazolam/triazolam oral, amiodarone, flecainide, simvastatin/lovastatin, rifampin)
relative: Cardiac conduction abnormalities or structural heart disease

preg: Limited human data. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk; if used, the boosted (ritonavir) regimen is required. Enroll in antiretroviral pregnancy registries.
lact: In settings where formula feeding is safe, breastfeeding is not recommended for HIV-positive mothers to avoid postnatal transmission of HIV regardless of drug therapy.
renal: No dose adjustment for mild to moderate renal impairment. Use with caution in severe renal impairment and end-stage renal disease as data are limited.
hepatic: Use with caution in mild to moderate hepatic impairment. Contraindicated in severe (decompensated) hepatic impairment. Monitor LFTs; hepatitis B/C co-infection increases risk of hepatotoxicity.

major: QT/PR-prolonging drugs (amiodarone, flecainide, dofetilide, class IA/III antiarrhythmics) - additive arrhythmia risk
Ergot derivatives - risk of severe peripheral vasospasm
Rifampin/rifabutin - reduced saquinavir levels and hepatotoxicity
interactions.food: Take within 2 hours after a meal; food markedly increases bioavailability
interactions.diagnostics: May raise glucose, lipids, and liver transaminases

serious: QT and PR interval prolongation / torsades de pointes
emergency: Torsades de pointes / syncope from arrhythmia

monitoring: ECG at baseline and during therapy (QT/PR intervals)
Serum potassium and magnesium (correct before starting)
Fasting blood glucose and lipid profile
HIV viral load and CD4 count for efficacy
counsel: Always take with ritonavir exactly as prescribed - this drug does not work alone
Take within 2 hours after a meal
Do not skip doses; missed doses promote resistance
Report fainting, palpitations, or irregular heartbeat immediately
Tell all prescribers you take saquinavir - it has many drug interactions
It controls but does not cure HIV; continue safe practices
pk: Antiviral effect over days to weeks; PK steady state within ~3-4 days
Plasma peak approximately 2-3 hours after a dose taken with food
Approximately 7 hours when boosted with ritonavir
Twice-daily dosing required to maintain levels
Store at room temperature 15-30 C; protect from moisture
pearls: Boxed-style warning: dose-dependent QT and PR prolongation - obtain baseline ECG and avoid in patients at risk of arrhythmia
Must always be boosted with low-dose ritonavir; never given as the sole protease inhibitor
Food dramatically increases absorption - dosing without food leads to subtherapeutic levels
Potent CYP3A4 interactions make a medication review mandatory before use
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered if it is not close to the next dose, then resume the usual schedule with food. Do not double up. Take saquinavir and ritonavir together.
overdose: Limited experience. Overdose may worsen QT/PR prolongation and gastrointestinal effects. Management is supportive with ECG monitoring, telemetry, electrolyte correction, and treatment of arrhythmias. Saquinavir is highly protein bound, so dialysis is unlikely to be beneficial.
